done_when: The generated client tests job allows 60 minutes like the full run, new repos get it at init and existing repos after sync

known.title: Follow-up: Correct the Forge-source timeout in the worker brief

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - a full test-suite run initializes a new client twice for the same budget check.
The new case calls `_new_client` and asserts both 60-minute job limits, just as `tests/test_full_run_time_limits.py:19-24` already does. The new test says existing tests assert the old limit, but this change updates that existing test to assert 60 minutes. The new case therefore detects no distinct regression, and the test-audit gate rejects duplicate invocations of the same contract. Consolidate the cases under one owner and map the proof list to it.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_client_tests_allow_sixty_minutes_on_init_and_sync[new]

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 2
The brief now says generated pull request and nightly jobs each get 60 minutes, but `src/forge/prcheck.py:366` still sets Forge's own pull request jobs to 45 minutes. `src/forge/worker.py:691` uses this same brief for Forge-source work, so a worker relying on the stated hour can still see a 46–60 minute test job canceled. Qualify the 60-minute pull request limit as applying to client repos.
findings.title: Follow-up: Correct the Forge-source timeout in the worker brief

why: A client's generated CI test job stops at 30 minutes, so a change that touches shared files and runs a large related set is cancelled with no output, while the nightly full run already allows 60
